meta.title: Indoor radon by municipality (STUK)

conventions.status: primary = STUK's own figures or the law; derived = our arithmetic; missing = STUK publishes no figure (value null).
conventions.units: Concentrations are annual averages in Bq/m³ as STUK computes them (a measurement made 1 Sep–31 May × 0.9); shares are percent of measured dwellings, as whole numbers exactly as STUK rounds them.

stuk-radon-municipalities.name: STUK: Pientalojen radonpitoisuudet kunnittain (radon in small-house dwellings by municipality), table radontilasto_pientalot_kunta_ja_koko_suomi_2023.xlsx
stuk-radon-municipalities.licence: None stated on the page or in the file. STUK's open data page (https://stuk.fi/avoin-data) applies CC BY 4.0 to the datasets in its open data service, but this table is not listed there; attribute STUK.
stuk-radon-municipalities.covers: Small-house dwellings (pientaloasunnot: detached, semi-detached and terraced houses) measured 1980–2023 in STUK's radon register (STUK's radon laboratory plus one commercial measurer's data). One value per dwelling: the highest measured there (e.g. before a radon repair). Municipal boundaries as of April 2024.
stuk-radon-municipalities.note: Only municipalities with at least 10 measured dwellings are listed; shares above 200/300/1000 Bq/m³ only where 30 or more were measured. Measured houses are not a random sample: people measure more where radon is known to be high, so these averages run higher than the average over all homes (STUK: about 94 Bq/m³ nationally). STUK: a home's radon cannot be inferred from the statistics; only a measurement tells. Columns: Kunta suomeksi, Mitattuja pientaloasuntoja, Keskiarvo, Mediaani, 200/300/1000 Bq/m3 ylitykset %, Kunta ruotsiksi. The same figures are on Sotkanet.

stm-1044-2018.name: Sosiaali- ja terveysministeriön asetus ionisoivasta säteilystä 1044/2018, 20 § (dwellings, 300 Bq/m³) and 21 § (new buildings, 200 Bq/m³)
stm-1044-2018.licence: Statutes are not protected by copyright (Tekijänoikeuslaki 9 §)
stm-1044-2018.note: Issued under the Radiation Act (Säteilylaki 859/2018). 20 §: the reference level for indoor radon in a dwelling and other living space is 300 Bq/m³, as an annual average; measure continuously for at least two months between the start of September and the end of May.

stuk-reference-levels.name: STUK: Asuntojen radonia koskevat viitearvot ja määräykset
stuk-reference-levels.note: Annual average = result of a measurement in the radon season (1 Sep–31 May) × 0.9; a year-long measurement gives the exact annual average. New buildings must be designed so that radon stays under 200 Bq/m³. The municipal health protection authority (terveydensuojelu) answers questions on dwellings.

stuk-radon-in-finland.name: STUK: Radon Suomessa
stuk-radon-in-finland.note: 'The average radon concentration in Finnish dwellings is about 94 Bq/m³' (all dwellings, not only measured small houses); about 4 mSv a year. STUK recommends measuring everywhere in Finland.

sf-municipalities-2026.name: Statistics Finland classification: Kunnat 2026 (kunta_1_20260101)
sf-municipalities-2026.note: 308 municipalities in 2026. Used only to check names and to list municipalities STUK leaves out; Pertunmaa is not in it (merged into Mäntyharju on 1 January 2025).

notes: Figures are for measured small-house dwellings 1980–2023, not all homes and not flats in blocks of flats. Measurement is voluntary and targeted at known radon areas, so a municipal average is higher than the true average over its homes; national: 228 Bq/m³ among measured small houses vs about 94 Bq/m³ over all dwellings.
Each dwelling counts once, with the highest value measured in it (often the pre-repair value), so the shares describe dwellings as first found, not after repairs.

Municipalities are as of April 2024. Pertunmaa merged into Mäntyharju on 1 January 2025; STUK still gives them separately. Mäntyharju's row is the old Mäntyharju; Pertunmaa's figures are under formerMunicipalities. We do not combine them.

25 municipalities with 10–29 measured dwellings have an average and median but no shares (null): STUK withholds shares below 30 dwellings because of large uncertainty. Averages from a few dozen houses are still uncertain.

7 municipalities are not in STUK's table at all (fewer than 10 measured dwellings): Brändö, Kumlinge, Kökar, Lumparland, Savukoski, Sottunga, Vårdö; they are present here with null values and status 'missing'.

STUK writes 'Maarianhamina' and 'Pedersöre'; Statistics Finland's 2026 names 'Maarianhamina - Mariehamn' and 'Pedersören kunta' are in aliases. Aliases also hold STUK's Swedish names where they differ from the Finnish one.
A municipal figure says nothing reliable about one house: STUK says the only way to know a home's radon is to measure it (at least two months between September and May).

referenceLevel.rule: The reference level for indoor radon in a dwelling is 300 Bq/m³ as an annual average; a new building must be designed and built so that it stays under 200 Bq/m³.

national.covers: STUK's 'Koko Suomi' row: all measured small-house dwellings in Finland 1980–2023 (not a representative sample).

allDwellings.covers: Average over all Finnish dwellings, as STUK states it ("noin 94 Bq/m³").
